# Important Notice for the Demo Data

[日本語](NOTICE_JA.md)

## Distribution status and rights

The distributor includes the two demo files in this Release for evaluation after confirming the following:

- `Original AI model Color.glb` was generated under a paid Hi3D plan and is cleared for publication and distribution in this package.
- `Reference.jpg` is original material that the distributor may publish and distribute; it is not a repost of a third party's work.

**Generated by Hi3D**

The demo files are separate materials from the `GPL-3.0-or-later` ChromaMatter software. ChromaMatter's `LICENSE.txt` does not apply to them. Inclusion in this package does not automatically grant recipients a right to redistribute, sell, repurpose, use as training data, or otherwise exploit the demo files separately. Unless applicable law permits it or the rights holder grants separate permission, use them only to evaluate ChromaMatter.

## Preserving provenance

`Reference.jpg` contains C2PA Content Credentials describing Google Generative AI and SynthID provenance. The distributed file preserves that information. Re-saving the image, stripping metadata, or converting it may prevent provenance verification and will change the SHA-256 recorded in [DEMO_DATA_MANIFEST.json](DEMO_DATA_MANIFEST.json).

## Independence and compatibility

ChromaMatter is an independent project. It is not an official, affiliated, or endorsed product of Hi3D, Google, Snapmaker, or any other third party. Product and service names are used only to describe compatibility, provenance, and the workflow.

Hi3D-style multipart GLB support is beta and unofficial. The node names in this GLB do not match the visible body regions, so do not use part names as proof of assembly position or print content. Even after solidification and 3MF export succeed, inspect geometry, materials, tool order, and the slice preview in Snapmaker Orca.

## Integrity verification

Expected sizes and SHA-256 values for the demo files are recorded in [DEMO_DATA_MANIFEST.json](DEMO_DATA_MANIFEST.json). Use the package-level `SOFTWARE_PACKAGE_SHA256.txt` as well when verifying the complete package.
